key_insight: GeoThinker replaces passive, global geometry fusion with active, task-driven geometry perception so that multimodal LLMs query and integrate only the spatial information they need, reducing semantic–geometry misalignment and redundancy.
problem_solved: Existing MLLM integration methods fuse 3D geometric features indiscriminately, causing misalignment between semantic and geometric signals and injecting redundant or noisy spatial information into reasoning.
method: Active geometry querying: the language/model side issues targeted probes to a 3D encoder to request only task-relevant geometric features instead of receiving a single global stream.
Selective integration & alignment: returned geometric patches are gated and aligned with semantic tokens (e.g., via attention or alignment losses) to ensure coherent cross-modal correspondence.
Iterative perception loop: geometry queries can be conditioned on intermediate reasoning steps so the model refines spatial information on demand rather than fusing everything up front.
impact: By turning geometry into an active, queryable resource, GeoThinker improves the efficiency and fidelity of spatial reasoning in multimodal systems—useful for robotics, AR/VR, and any application requiring precise 3D-aware language understanding.

paper_title: Thinking with Geometry: Active Geometry Integration for Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Tao Tang, Kun Xiang, Zihan Guo
